description: Bird dog guide: reach opposite arm and leg with a flat back to train back muscles, glutes and deep core. Covers mistakes plus easier and harder versions.
intro: The bird dog is done on hands and knees: you reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back while keeping your trunk still. It trains the back muscles, glutes and deep core to hold the spine and pelvis steady. It supports the pelvic floor rather than training it directly.
feel: You should feel your back muscles and the glute of the lifted leg working, with a steady low effort in your belly. You should not feel your lower back sag, your hips twist or your neck strain. Imagine a cup of water on your lower back: if it would spill as you reach, the arm or leg is going too high.

mistakes.wrong: Lifting the leg too high and arching the back
mistakes.right: Reach the leg back, not up, and stop at hip height so the lower back stays flat.

mistakes.wrong: Shifting the hips toward the standing leg
mistakes.right: Keep weight even and hips square to the floor. Shorten the reach if they tip.
Breathe out as you reach and breathe in as you return.

easier: Move only the leg or only the arm, keeping the other three points down, or slide the leg back along the floor.
harder: Hold the reach for five seconds, move more slowly, or add a gentle Kegel on the exhale followed by full relaxation.
who: Useful for desk workers with a stiff back, people over 40, lifters who want a stable trunk, and anyone who needs low-impact core work.
skip: If your wrists hurt, use fists or forearms. Check with a doctor or physiotherapist first if you have acute back pain, recent abdominal or pelvic surgery, or knees that hurt when kneeling. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: Is the bird dog good for lower back pain?
faq.a: It is often used in back rehab because it trains stability with little load on the spine. If you have pain, ask a physiotherapist whether it suits you.

faq.q: How long should I hold each bird dog?
faq.a: Start with a one or two second pause and build to five seconds once your back stays flat.
